titulo: Study Guide 2 — Informational texts, comparatives and adverbs

bloques.titulo: What you will learn this week

bloques.html:
• Read an informational text (science or history) and find the main idea of each paragraph.
  • Use text features: title, headings, bold words, captions and fact boxes.
  • Work out the meaning of a new word from the context (the words around it).
  • Compare things with comparatives (bigger, more careful) and superlatives (the biggest, the most careful).
  • Use adverbs to say how something happens (quietly, carefully, fast).
  • Write a paragraph of 5-6 sentences with a topic sentence, details and a closing sentence.

Reading an informational text

An informational text gives facts about a real topic. It is organized to help you find information:

Text feature What it does
Title Tells the topic of the whole text
Headings Tell what each section is about (like mini-titles)
Bold words Important words, usually defined in the text
Caption / fact box Extra information next to a picture or in a box ("Did you know?")

Main idea of a paragraph: what the paragraph is mostly about, in one sentence. It is often the first sentence. The other sentences are details that explain or prove it. Ask yourself: "If I had to say this paragraph in one sentence, what would I say?"

Vocabulary in context: when you find a new word, do not stop. Look for: a definition right after it ("...called a lodge, a dome of sticks..."), an example, or a contrast ("...dry and warm, even in the coldest winter"). Then replace the word with your guess and check that the sentence still makes sense.

Grammar box — Comparatives and superlatives

Type of adjective Comparative (two things) Superlative (three or more)
Short (1 syllable): tall, fast, cold taller than, faster, colder the tallest, fastest, coldest
Short ending in one vowel + consonant: big, hot, flat bigger, hotter, flatter the biggest, hottest, flattest
Ending in -y: happy, busy, heavy happier, busier, heavier the happiest, busiest, heaviest
Long (2+ syllables): careful, dangerous, interesting more careful than, more dangerous the most careful, the most dangerous
Irregular good → better · bad → worse · far → farther the best · the worst · the farthest

Never mix the two forms: "more bigger" and "most fastest" are wrong. Equal things: as ... as → A beaver is as heavy as a ten-year-old child.

Adverbs of manner say how an action happens. Most are adjective + -ly: quiet → quietly, careful → carefully, slow → slowly, easy → easily (y → i), gentle → gently. Irregular: fast → fast, hard → hard, good → well. Adjectives describe nouns (a quiet beaver); adverbs describe verbs (the beaver swam quietly).

Read this short text and follow the examples.

The Araucaria: A Living Fossil

An ancient tree. The araucaria, or monkey-puzzle tree, has lived in the mountains of southern Chile and Argentina for more than 200 million years. That means it was already growing when dinosaurs walked the Earth. Scientists call it a living fossil: a species that has changed very little over millions of years.

Slow but strong. An araucaria grows slowly, only a few centimeters a year, but it can live for 1,000 years and reach 50 meters. Its trunk is covered in thick, hard bark that protects it from fire. Its sharp, triangular leaves stop animals from climbing it.

A sacred tree. For the Mapuche people, the araucaria (pewen) is sacred. Its seeds, called piñones, have been an important food for centuries. Today the tree is protected by law, and it is a national monument of Chile.

Did you know? One araucaria can produce more than 200 kilograms of seeds in a good year.

Example 1 (main idea). What is the main idea of the paragraph "Slow but strong"? → The heading helps: the paragraph is about how the tree grows slowly but is very strong and well protected. Answer: The araucaria grows slowly but is strong and well protected against fire and animals.

Example 2 (text features). Which feature would you use to find quickly the part about the Mapuche? → The headings ("A sacred tree").

Example 3 (vocabulary in context). What is a "living fossil"? → The text defines it right after the bold word: "a species that has changed very little over millions of years".

Example 4 (why the author included something). Why does the author include the fact box? → To give a surprising fact (200 kg of seeds) that supports the idea that the seeds are an important food.

Example 5 (comparative). The araucaria is (old) than the dinosaurs' first cousins. → short adjective → older than.

Example 6 (superlative). It is one of the (interesting) trees in Chile. → long adjective → most interesting.

Example 7 (adverb). The tree grows (slow). → how does it grow? → slowly.

Example 8 (paragraph). A good paragraph has: a topic sentence (what it is about) → 3-4 detail sentences → a closing sentence. Example: Dogs are better pets than fish. First, a dog can play with you, but a fish just swims. Second, dogs are more loyal: they wait for you at the door. Finally, a dog is more fun on holidays because it can come with you. For all these reasons, I would always choose a dog.

Read the text and answer questions 1 to 6.

Polar Bears: Giants of the Ice

The biggest bear. The polar bear is the largest bear in the world. An adult male can weigh 600 kilograms, as much as a small car. It lives in the Arctic, in Canada, Russia, Greenland and Norway, where the sea is frozen for most of the year.

Built for the cold. Under its white fur, a polar bear's skin is black, which helps it absorb heat from the sun. A thick layer of fat, called blubber, keeps it warm when it swims in freezing water. Its huge paws work like snowshoes on the ice and like paddles in the sea.

A hunter on thin ice. Polar bears hunt seals by waiting next to holes in the ice. But the Arctic is getting warmer, and the ice melts earlier every year. With less ice, bears have less time to hunt and must swim longer distances. Scientists worry that the polar bear's future depends on how much the planet warms.

Did you know? A polar bear can smell a seal from one kilometer away.
What is the main idea of the paragraph "Built for the cold"?
What does "blubber" mean? How do you know?
Which text feature tells you what each paragraph is about?
According to the text, why is less ice a problem for polar bears?
Why does the author include the "Did you know?" box?
Is the sentence "Polar bears are the most beautiful animals" a fact from the text? Why or why not?
Grammar.
Write the comparative and superlative: a) cold b) big c) heavy d) dangerous e) good
Complete: A polar bear is (heavy) than a beaver. The Arctic is the (cold) place a bear can live.
Correct the mistake: The polar bear is more bigger than the brown bear.
Write the adverb: a) quick → b) careful → c) easy → d) good →
Choose adjective or adverb: The bear moved (slow / slowly) across the ice. The ice was (thin / thinly).
Make one sentence with "as ... as": a beaver / a ten-year-old child / heavy.
Writing.
Write a paragraph of 5-6 sentences comparing two seasons (for example, summer and winter). Use a topic sentence, two comparatives, one superlative and one adverb. Finish with a closing sentence.
Listening and speaking practice (ask an adult).
Ask an adult to read you a short article about an animal or a volcano twice. Then say: "The text was about . The most important idea was ."
Explain step by step how to make your favorite sandwich. Use first, next, then, after that, finally.
1. The polar bear's body is adapted to live in the cold (black skin, blubber, huge paws).
1. A thick layer of fat; the text defines it right after the word: "A thick layer of fat, called blubber".
1. The headings.
1. With less ice, bears have less time to hunt seals and must swim longer distances.
1. To give a surprising fact that shows how good the bear's sense of smell is (it supports the idea that it is a great hunter).
1. No. It is an opinion, and the text does not say it. The text gives facts (size, weight, where it lives).
1. a) colder / the coldest b) bigger / the biggest c) heavier / the heaviest d) more dangerous / the most dangerous e) better / the best.
1. heavier · coldest.
1. The polar bear is bigger than the brown bear.
1. a) quickly b) carefully c) easily d) well.
1. slowly · thin.
1. A beaver is as heavy as a ten-year-old child.
1. Check: topic sentence, 5-6 sentences, two comparatives (hotter, longer, more fun...), one superlative (the best, the coldest...), one adverb (slowly, happily...), closing sentence.
Items 14 and 15: the adult checks that you said the topic and the main idea, and that your steps were in order with the linking words.
